plain: Legal control over a person or thing, such as a child or prisoner

webster.text: A keeping; a guarding; care, watch, inspection, for keeping, preservation or security.

more.text: Defense from a foe; preservation; security.

example.quote: A father's right to the custody of his own children being founded in law on the right of guardianship, this being taken away, they may of course be severed from him, and put by the authority of the court, into more orthodox hands.
example.cite: Thomas Jefferson, Notes on the State of Virginia, Query XVII (Religion) (1802 ed.)
